ic.a.leverage.evidence: Interest cover of {cover}: the cash flow carries the interest comfortably.
ic.a.leverage.concede: I will leave the room to raise in the final round unused.
ic.a.leverage.push_back: On today's lending terms this is market standard.
ic.a.price.evidence: The price is inside the outside adviser's range.
ic.a.price.concede: I will not raise the price in the final round.
ic.a.price.push_back: It is a competitive auction. Below this we do not win.
ic.a.interest_cover.evidence: Rate sensitivity is already in the model.
ic.a.interest_cover.concede: I will narrow the room to raise and carry less debt.
ic.a.interest_cover.push_back: Rates have peaked. They only go down from here.
ic.a.no_financial_dd.evidence: The IM ties to the audited accounts.
ic.a.no_financial_dd.concede: I will have the financial report in before we bid.
ic.a.no_financial_dd.push_back: Diligence costs too much for a company this size.
ic.a.no_commercial_dd.evidence: I called five of the top customers myself.
ic.a.no_commercial_dd.concede: I will finish commercial diligence before we bid.
ic.a.no_commercial_dd.push_back: We know this sector better than anyone.
ic.a.no_operational_dd.evidence: Capex has been steady for years.
ic.a.no_operational_dd.concede: I will finish the site visit before we bid.
ic.a.no_legal_dd.evidence: I have seen the registry and the main contracts.
ic.a.no_legal_dd.concede: I will finish legal diligence before we bid.
ic.a.inventory_days.evidence: Slow turns are normal for the trade.
ic.a.inventory_days.concede: Financial diligence will check the inventory before we bid.
ic.a.thin_returns.evidence: With the 100-day plan the IRR rises.
ic.a.thin_returns.concede: I will narrow the room to raise and protect the entry price.
ic.a.thin_returns.push_back: This deal is about the multiple of money, not IRR.
ic.a.multiple_reliance.evidence: The adviser's trading comparables support this price.
ic.a.multiple_reliance.concede: I will not raise the price in the final round.
ic.a.downside.evidence: With cover of {cover} it holds in the downside.
ic.a.downside.concede: I will narrow the room to raise and borrow less.
ic.a.no_plan.evidence: We will write the plan with management after closing.
ic.a.no_plan.concede: I will pay less and settle the plan after closing.
ic.a.layoffs_in_union_shop.evidence: I have already talked to the union.
ic.a.layoffs_in_union_shop.concede: I will price conservatively and lean less on the cuts.
ic.a.layoffs_in_union_shop.push_back: Without the cuts there is no return.
ic.a.fund_concentration.evidence: A co-investor brings us inside the limit.
ic.a.fund_concentration.concede: I will narrow the room to raise and write a smaller check.
ic.a.fund_concentration.push_back: Good deals deserve a big bet.
ic.a.open_issue.evidence: It is priced in: we are below the valuation midpoint.
ic.a.open_issue.concede: I will narrow the room to raise.
ic.a.open_issue.push_back: Every company has issues like this.
ic.a.exit.evidence: The market is good and growth beats the industry. Strategics will bid.
ic.a.exit.concede: I will assume an exit at the entry multiple.
ic.a.value_creation.concede: I will pay less and prove it in the execution.
ic.a.cycle.evidence: Cover of {cover} carries it through a recession.
ic.a.cycle.concede: I will narrow the room to raise and take less cycle risk.
ic.title: Investment committee
ic.verdict.approved: Approved. You may bid at this price.
ic.verdict.held: Held. Revise the offer and bring it back.
ic.verdict.rejected: Rejected. This deal needs a rethink.
ic.conditions: Condition: {streams} diligence done before the bid
ic.cut: Room to raise cut by {pct} points
ic.sitting: The committee is sitting. Three partners have questions.
msg.committee_convened.title: {company}: IC meeting
msg.committee_convened.body: The committee is sitting. Answer its questions in the deal room.
msg.owner_considering.title: {company}: the owner is considering
msg.bank_feedback.title: {company}: the seller's bank
msg.bank_feedback.leading.price: You lead for now. Prices can move again in the final round.
msg.bank_feedback.leading.certainty: You lead. The seller values certainty of closing.
msg.bank_feedback.close.price: You are close to the lead. Price decides it.
msg.bank_feedback.close.certainty: It is close. The seller weighs certainty as much as price.
msg.bank_feedback.behind.price: You are well behind. Look at the price again.
msg.bank_feedback.behind.certainty: You are behind, but the relationship with the seller can close some of it.
block.owner_considering: The owner is considering the proposal.
error.condition_open: A report the IC asked for is not in yet.
ic.a.no_protection.evidence: I have known the owner for years and diligence found nothing.
ic.a.no_protection.concede: From the next minority deal on, we go in with preferred shares.
ic.a.no_protection.push_back: Ask for preferred and the owner walks. These are the terms that get us in.
talk.think.1: A good proposal. Let me talk it over with the family; you will hear from me in a month or two.
talk.think.2: I see the numbers. I will hear the accountant and the bank first, then give you an answer.
talk.think.3: I’ll talk it over with the kids at the weekend. It isn’t mine alone to decide.
talk.think.4: My tax adviser wants to run the numbers first. Give me a month or two.
ic.open.1: Let’s begin. Today’s item is an acquisition at {ev}. Short questions, answers in numbers.
ic.open.2: This is a {ev} deal. I trust everyone has read the pack; straight in.
ic.open.3: Whatever is said in this room, we repeat to our investors. {ev} — make your case.
ic.open.4: Let’s finish before the coffee goes cold. You want to pay {ev}? First question.
ic.q.leverage.1: Leverage is {leverage}. One bad year of EBITDA and we trip the covenants. Can you justify this debt?
ic.q.leverage.2: {leverage} would be among the heaviest in our book. Why can this company carry it?
ic.q.leverage.3: Just because lenders offer {leverage}, must we take it? The company repays it, not us.
ic.q.price.1: That is {premium} against our own valuation. Why pay it?
ic.q.price.2: We pay {premium} over our own number. When do we earn that back?
ic.q.price.3: Aren’t we caught up in auction fever? That’s {premium} against our valuation.
ic.q.interest_cover.1: Interest cover is only {cover}. What happens if rates go up once more?
ic.q.interest_cover.2: At {cover} of interest cover, one point of rates chokes us. Did you consider a hedge?
ic.q.interest_cover.3: {cover}. After capex, is there cash left for interest?
ic.q.no_financial_dd.1: No financial diligence and we are to trust the numbers? Who checked inventory and receivables?
ic.q.no_financial_dd.2: Are we buying on the seller’s numbers alone? One audit opinion isn’t enough.
ic.q.no_financial_dd.3: Who adjusted the adjusted EBITDA? None of our people have looked.
ic.q.no_commercial_dd.1: Nobody has tested customers or the market. What backs the growth case?
ic.q.no_commercial_dd.2: Do you know the top five customers by name? Will they still buy next year?
ic.q.no_commercial_dd.3: That market growth rate looks copied from the adviser’s deck. Did you check anything yourself?
ic.q.no_operational_dd.1: Nobody has walked the plant. We would buy without knowing the state of the equipment?
ic.q.no_operational_dd.2: What’s the plant running at? If you don’t know, we don’t buy.
ic.q.no_operational_dd.3: So we spend millions without one site visit.
ic.q.no_legal_dd.1: Legal diligence is missing. Contracts, litigation, permits?
ic.q.no_legal_dd.2: Did anyone check the key contracts for change-of-control clauses?
ic.q.no_legal_dd.3: One lawsuit and the return is gone. I won’t sign without a legal review.
ic.q.inventory_days.1: Inventory days run long for the industry. Can we take the inventory on the books at face value?
ic.q.inventory_days.2: That inventory in the warehouse — can it actually be sold?
ic.q.inventory_days.3: With inventory days this long, working capital eats the cash. How did you set the peg?
ic.q.thin_returns.1: The base case IRR is {irr}. That is below our hurdle.
ic.q.thin_returns.2: At {irr} we’d do better buying bonds. Why take this risk?
ic.q.thin_returns.3: If the base case is {irr}, the downside case is a loss.
ic.q.multiple_reliance.1: Growth is industry average and the price is a premium. Does this only work if the multiple expands at exit?
ic.q.multiple_reliance.2: Who promises we get today’s multiple at exit?
ic.q.multiple_reliance.3: Deals that lean on the multiple are the first to fall when rates rise.
ic.q.downside.1: If EBITDA falls by a fifth this debt does not hold. Have you run the downside?
ic.q.downside.2: Lose one customer and EBITDA falls that far. What do we tell the lenders then?
ic.q.downside.3: As someone who remembers 2009: in the worst case, how much of our equity survives?
ic.q.no_plan.1: The 100-day plan is empty. What do we do on day one?
ic.q.no_plan.2: Buying without a plan is just holding shares. What are our fees for, then?
ic.q.no_plan.3: What will you tell the CEO in the first hundred days?
ic.q.layoffs_in_union_shop.1: The plan cuts heads in a shop that is {union} unionized. Who answers for the strike?
ic.q.layoffs_in_union_shop.2: Restructuring where {union} are unionised makes the papers. Remember some of our LPs are pension funds.
ic.q.layoffs_in_union_shop.3: With {union} unionised, negotiation alone takes six months. Is that cost in the plan?
ic.q.fund_concentration.1: Equity of {equity} is over the per-deal limit of {limit}. What do we tell the LPs?
ic.q.fund_concentration.2: That puts {equity} in one basket. The {limit} limit isn’t decoration.
ic.q.fund_concentration.3: At {equity} this one deal decides the fund. Have you looked for co-investors?
ic.q.open_issue.1: Diligence found {issues}. Is it in the price?
ic.q.open_issue.2: We know about {issues} and buy anyway. Is there protection in the contract?
ic.q.open_issue.3: {issues} only grows later. Take it off the price now.
ic.q.exit.1: Who buys this from us in five years?
ic.q.exit.2: Will strategics queue for this, or will we be passing it to the next fund?
ic.q.exit.3: Will it be big enough to list? If not, name three buyers.
ic.q.value_creation.1: What changes at this company once we own it?
ic.q.value_creation.2: This company grows this much without us. What do we add?
ic.q.value_creation.3: As the operating partner: if I walk into that plant next month, what do I change first?
ic.q.cycle.1: We are in a {phase}. What happens to this company in a recession?
ic.q.cycle.2: Buy in {phase}, sell in the next phase. What does this company look like then?
ic.q.cycle.3: If we’re in {phase}, aren’t we getting in too late?
ic.q.no_protection.1: No control, and common shares. If the owner gets it wrong, what protects our money?
ic.q.no_protection.2: A minority in common shares: if the owner pays no dividend, we just wait.
ic.q.no_protection.3: No board seat, no preference. What cards do we hold?
ic.r.evidence.yes.3: Solid work. I withdraw my concern.
ic.r.evidence.no.1: That is thin. It does not answer it.
ic.r.evidence.no.2: That’s just the seller’s deck read back to me.
ic.r.evidence.no.3: I asked for numbers, not adjectives.
ic.r.concede.yes.1: On that condition, fine. Minute it.
ic.r.concede.yes.2: Fine. That condition goes in the minutes.
ic.r.concede.yes.3: You know when to give. I can support that.
ic.r.concede.no.1: A condition alone is not enough.
ic.r.concede.no.2: This isn’t something a concession covers.
ic.r.concede.no.3: Adding a condition doesn’t make the risk go away.
ic.r.push_back.yes.1: …All right. I will trust your judgment.
ic.r.push_back.yes.2: If you’re that sure, go ahead. The result carries your name.
ic.r.push_back.yes.3: I’ll grant you nerve. I’ll trust you this time.
ic.r.push_back.no.1: That is not an answer. I am against.
ic.r.push_back.no.3: Being loud doesn’t win in this room.
ic.verdict.approved.say.1: Congratulations. Holding the price is your job now.
ic.verdict.approved.say.2: Approved. Don’t forget today’s questions after we own it.
ic.verdict.approved.say.3: I hope it’s a good one. This name will be in a lot of LP letters.
ic.verdict.held.say.1: The direction is fine. Fix the structure and come back next month.
ic.verdict.held.say.2: I can’t sign this version. Fix what we raised and that’s it.
ic.verdict.held.say.3: There’s still time. Better than rushing into a bad deal.
ic.verdict.rejected.say.1: Let this one go. Another deal will come.
ic.verdict.rejected.say.2: It isn’t a bad company. It’s the wrong one for this fund.
ic.verdict.rejected.say.3: A no goes in the record too. Write down what you missed.
